title: Coherence of the proved comparisons
statement:
The operations in [def-fix-six-functor-datum] and their proved
comparison maps satisfy identity, composition, exchange and projection
coherence. The elementary coefficient comparisons of
[lem-fix-operation-reduction] extend to general constructible
finite-Tor internal Hom by [thm-coef-finite-hom], to integral
internal Hom by [lem-coef-integral-hom-reduction], and to finite
coefficient-field extensions by [lem-coef-integral-finite-extension].
Exceptional comparisons on these constructible domains are
[lem-coef-finite-exceptional], [prop-coef-integral-exceptional-adjoint], [lem-coef-rational-operations]. Smooth orientation and the site-perfect Poincare pairing have
the additional compatibilities of
[thm-pur-finite-reduction-of-purity], [thm-pod-finite-reduction].
At field coefficients these maps are Weil-equivariant, with the purity
compatibilities of [prop-pur-weil-equivariance-compatibilities].

proof.text: Identity and horizontal/vertical exchange pasting, including refinement compatibility, are [fix-lem-exchanges]. Finite compact-support composition is [thm-sf-comp-composition]; [lem-sf-completed-shriek-composition-laws] supplies its system, completed and field unit/associativity laws with the required local uniform bounds.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sf-finite-projection-exchange-transposes] to the finite projection diamond and identity case. Its open restrictions and proper counit transposes identify the two routes. Apply [lem-sf-completed-projection-exchange-realization] for the system equality, its completed realization and field passage. The projection isomorphism, its pentagon, proper coincidence and refinement compatibility are those of [fix-prop-projection-formula].

source.place: Assembly 2; full returned argument and extraction map retained in report.md

proof.text: The isomorphisms of [thm-coef-finite-hom], [lem-coef-integral-hom-reduction] and [lem-coef-integral-finite-extension], with the overlap equations of [lem-sf-general-hom-comparison-cocycles], give identity, successive quotient, integral-to-finite and finite-extension equations by their evaluation transposes. Use both-variable finite-Tor hypotheses for finite Hom, and its stated overlap for successive integral reduction. [lem-sf-constructible-exceptional-mate-cocycles] identifies these transpositions under the specified constructible adjunctions and gives the exceptional identity and composition equations.

source.place: Assembly 3; full returned argument and extraction map retained in report.md

proof.text: On the exceptionally admissible domain apply [lem-sf-verdier-hom-chain-composition]. Its representing Hom chain identifies the proved Verdier map, and its substitution equation gives composition and identity. The same chain commutes term by term with coefficient comparisons. This adds no duality/pullback or preservation assertion.

source.place: Assembly 4; full returned argument and extraction map retained in report.md

proof.text: Use the actual orientation reduction square of [thm-pur-finite-reduction-of-purity] and the site-perfect pairing square of [thm-pod-finite-reduction], retaining their smooth structure-map hypotheses. Evaluation is preserved by [lem-fix-operation-reduction]. Composing these commuting squares gives the pairing comparison: if $b'u=vb$ and $c'v=wc$, then $(c'b')u=w(cb)$.

source.place: Assembly 5; full returned argument and extraction map retained in report.md

proof.text: For geometric fibres over the finite base field, [lem-fix-weil-operations] gives algebraic-map equivariance and [cor-coef-verdier-weil-equivariance] gives general duality and exceptional equivariance. Compose with the actual geometric and scheme-Frobenius purity/trace squares of [thm-pur-weil-equivariance-of-purity-and-trace], [prop-pur-weil-equivariance-scheme-frobenius] and [prop-pur-weil-equivariance-compatibilities]. Equivariance of composites follows from $\varphi_CF(ba)=b\varphi_BF(a)=ba\varphi_A$. Thus the orientation-induced pairing is equivariant on its stated domain.

proof.text:
The identity and pasting equations are [fix-lem-exchanges].
The projection diamonds and associativity are
[fix-prop-projection-formula]; taking adjoint mates gives the
corresponding equations for [fix-cor-verdier-exchange].
The maps used here are tensor reassociation, evaluation, and adjunction
units and counits, whose coefficient comparisons are proved in
[lem-fix-operation-reduction]. The general Hom comparisons
[thm-coef-finite-hom], [lem-coef-integral-hom-reduction], [lem-coef-integral-finite-extension]
are defined by the same evaluation maps. The exceptional comparisons
[lem-coef-finite-exceptional] and those of [sk-prop-scalar-six] for the
adjoint of [sk-thm-existence]
preserve units and counits, so their mates satisfy the same equations.
Their Weil structures are [lem-fix-weil-operations], with
general duality equivariance given by [cor-coef-verdier-weil-equivariance]. The geometric orientation is supplied
separately by [thm-pur-finite-reduction-of-purity] and
[prop-pur-weil-equivariance-compatibilities]; composing it with
evaluation gives the pairing comparison [thm-pod-finite-reduction].
Thus coherence is inherited from the individual maps on the stated
domains, without an additional preservation or biduality assertion.
